<div class="toolbox-kind">Resource · verified catalog guide 2026-10-04</div>

## Start with the measurement

Record these before opening a catalog:

- area of interest and whether one scene must cover it;
- target date/range and acceptable temporal offset;
- maximum useful cloud cover;
- required spatial and temporal resolution;
- measurement: true color, reflectance, surface temperature, water vapour, active fire or radar response;
- whether the output is for visual evidence or quantitative analysis.

The same event can require two products: a broad, frequent product to locate the right day and a finer product for the final map.

## Product decision table

| Need | Start with | Resolution / cadence | Catalog | Main trade-off |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Detailed optical land image or true color | Sentinel-2 Level-2A | 10 m RGB/NIR; nominal 5-day constellation revisit | Copernicus Data Space | Clouds; one tile is roughly 100 × 100 km |
| Optical surface reflectance and a long archive | Landsat Collection 2 Level-2 | 30 m; lower temporal density | USGS EarthExplorer | Finer historical depth, fewer clear observations |
| Land surface temperature at city/landscape scale | Landsat Collection 2 Level-2 Surface Temperature | 30 m product grid | USGS EarthExplorer | Cloud-sensitive and less frequent |
| Daily land surface temperature | MOD11A1 (Terra) / MYD11A1 (Aqua) | Daily, 1 km | NASA Earthdata Search | Coarse pixels; use QA layers |
| Broad, frequent true-color context | MODIS or VIIRS Corrected Reflectance | About 250 m browse imagery, near daily global context | NASA Worldview | Good for event discovery, not detailed local analysis |
| Total precipitable water vapour | MOD05_L2 (Terra) / MYD05_L2 (Aqua) | Swath product, 1 km and 5 km retrievals | NASA Earthdata Search | Specialized variables, swath geometry and QA |
| Active-fire locations | FIRMS VIIRS / MODIS | VIIRS 375 m; MODIS 1 km; near real time | NASA FIRMS | Detection pixels are not exact fire perimeters |
| Optical land image with persistent cloud | Sentinel-1 GRD radar | Mission/mode dependent | Copernicus Data Space | Radar is not true color and needs different interpretation |
| Frequent LST or fire-radiative-power product | Sentinel-3 SLSTR LST / FRP | Coarser, frequent thematic product | Copernicus Data Space | Better cadence and coverage, much coarser detail |

Nominal resolution or revisit does not guarantee a usable observation. Clouds, orbit geometry, daylight, latency and product QA still decide whether the scene works.

## Official discovery tools

### Copernicus / Sentinel

- [Copernicus Browser](https://browser.dataspace.copernicus.eu/): visual search and preview.
- [Copernicus STAC Browser](https://browser.stac.dataspace.copernicus.eu/): inspect collections, items and assets.
- [Current STAC API](https://stac.dataspace.copernicus.eu/v1/): programmatic discovery.
- [STAC documentation](https://documentation.dataspace.copernicus.eu/APIs/STAC.html): filters, queryables, sorting and current collection IDs.

The current Sentinel-2 collection ID is `sentinel-2-l2a`. Use L2A for bottom-of-atmosphere surface reflectance; L1C is top-of-atmosphere reflectance.

### NASA / MODIS / VIIRS / Aqua

- [NASA Worldview](https://worldview.earthdata.nasa.gov/): visually inspect dates and broad imagery quickly.
- [NASA Earthdata Search](https://search.earthdata.nasa.gov/): find collections and granules, then download source data.
- [NASA FIRMS](https://firms.modaps.eosdis.nasa.gov/): active-fire detections and downloads.

Worldview is excellent for answering “which day looks useful?” Earthdata Search is the normal next step when the underlying scientific product—not a rendered snapshot—is required.

### Landsat

- [USGS EarthExplorer](https://earthexplorer.usgs.gov/): spatial/temporal search and download.
- [Landsat Collection 2 Level-2 products](https://www.usgs.gov/landsat-missions/landsat-collection-2-level-2-science-products): surface reflectance and surface temperature documentation.

## Search Sentinel-2 with STAC

This verified example searches a bbox near Geneva, a date range and item-level cloud cover. Discovery does not require downloading full products.

```{python}
#| eval: false
import requests

stac_search = "https://stac.dataspace.copernicus.eu/v1/search"


def search_sentinel2(bbox, start, end, max_cloud=20, limit=100):
    params = {
        "collections": "sentinel-2-l2a",
        "bbox": ",".join(map(str, bbox)),
        "datetime": f"{start}T00:00:00Z/{end}T23:59:59Z",
        "filter": f"eo:cloud_cover <= {max_cloud}",
        "sortby": "properties.datetime",
        "limit": limit,
    }

    items = []
    url = stac_search
    while url:
        response = requests.get(url, params=params, timeout=60)
        response.raise_for_status()
        page = response.json()
        items.extend(page["features"])

        next_link = next(
            (link for link in page["links"] if link["rel"] == "next"),
            None,
        )
        url = next_link["href"] if next_link else None
        params = None

    return items


items = search_sentinel2(
    bbox=[6.05, 46.10, 6.25, 46.30],
    start="2025-08-01",
    end="2025-08-15",
    max_cloud=20,
)

[
    {
        "id": item["id"],
        "datetime": item["properties"]["datetime"],
        "cloud_cover": item["properties"].get("eo:cloud_cover"),
        "platform": item["properties"].get("platform"),
    }
    for item in items
]
```

The live test returned four L2A items with cloud-cover metadata between approximately 0% and 9%. Each exposed individual 10 m bands, a `TCI_10m` true-color asset, scene classification (`SCL_20m`) and product metadata.

## Prefer complete coverage, not only low cloud

`eo:cloud_cover` describes the full Sentinel tile, not just the area of interest. First rank scenes by how much of the requested area they cover, then inspect clouds over the area itself.

```{python}
#| eval: false
import geopandas as gpd
import pandas as pd
from shapely.geometry import box, shape

aoi = gpd.GeoDataFrame(
    {"name": ["area"]},
    geometry=[box(6.05, 46.10, 6.25, 46.30)],
    crs=4326,
)

candidates = gpd.GeoDataFrame(
    {
        "id": [item["id"] for item in items],
        "datetime": [item["properties"]["datetime"] for item in items],
        "cloud_cover": [
            item["properties"].get("eo:cloud_cover") for item in items
        ],
    },
    geometry=[shape(item["geometry"]) for item in items],
    crs=4326,
)

local_crs = aoi.estimate_utm_crs()
aoi_projected = aoi.to_crs(local_crs).geometry.iloc[0]
candidates = candidates.to_crs(local_crs)
candidates["coverage"] = (
    candidates.geometry.intersection(aoi_projected).area
    / aoi_projected.area
)

candidates.sort_values(
    ["coverage", "cloud_cover", "datetime"],
    ascending=[False, True, True],
)[["id", "datetime", "cloud_cover", "coverage"]]
```

For a large area, no single tile may cover everything. Group candidates by acquisition date/orbit and compare the number of scenes needed rather than simply choosing the clearest individual tile.

## Inspect assets before downloading

For a quick visual check, `TCI_10m` is the rendered true-color asset. For analysis, select the original bands explicitly:

- B04, B03, B02: red, green, blue at 10 m;
- B08: near-infrared at 10 m;
- B11/B12: shortwave infrared at 20 m;
- SCL: scene classification at 20 m for clouds, shadows, snow and other classes.

Do not treat a thumbnail or true-color composite as surface-reflectance analysis data. Save the selected item JSON or at least the collection, item ID, acquisition time, processing level and asset URLs with the project.

## Checks before committing to a download

1. Does the footprint cover the whole area, or how many items are required?
2. Is the timestamp acquisition time rather than processing/update time?
3. Is cloud cover acceptable over the area itself, including shadows?
4. Is the variable physical (for example LST) or only a visualization layer?
5. Are units, scale factors, nodata and QA flags documented?
6. Is the spatial resolution native, or has a coarse band merely been resampled?
7. For fire data, is the product an active detection, burned area or ordinary imagery?

After acquisition, use the [raster reference](../snippets/raster.qmd) for inspection, crop/mask, calculations and export.
